# Tŷ Mawr — The Great House Farm Story — llms.txt

> The true story of the Williams/Buckler family and Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan, Wales, in 102 scenes across 8 acts with a prologue and epilogue, in strict date order.
> Every scene is drawn from the Great House Farm Wiki evidence catalogue (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/) and carries its evidence links.
> Structured JSON (acts, cast, scenes, evidence, stable ids): https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/api/timeline.json
> Printable script (static HTML, no JavaScript needed): https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/story/
> Storyboard: https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/?view=storyboard · Cast: https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/?view=cast · Any scene: https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/?event=<id>

## About

The Williams family lived at Great House Farm, beside St Dochdwy's Church, Llandough, for generations (by the family's account since 1667). The family's case is that the farm was two parcels: the house parcel (Parcel A), which passed out of the Bute estate to Daniel Thomas in 1877 and became the family's freehold when quarrying ended in 1928, and the eastern fields (Parcel B), which went to Western Ground Rents in 1938 and to BP. The possession cases of 1955, 1962, 1974 and BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 decided possession; none of them examined the documents that bear on the family's title to the house parcel. BP demolished the farmhouse on 6 December 1988, the morning after Cadw declined to list it, before it could be fully recorded. In 1994 an early-medieval cemetery of 1,026 burials was excavated on the site. Since 2025 the family have been recovering the missing records, and Cadw, Heneb and HM Land Registry's Independent Complaints Reviewer are now investigating. The family's case is that fraud and concealment kept the title documents from the courts, so the case can be reopened.

Truth labels follow the Wiki: documented fact, family evidence, reconstruction, legal inference and unresolved. The 1978–79 Llandough Roman Villa is a separate site south of the church.

## Full Timeline

102 scenes, in strict date order.

### P.1 (1). c. AD 650 — The church beside the house

Prologue: The Root · Scene id: ghf-06500101-1 · Date: 0650-01-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Family account

Long before there is a farm, there is a church. St Dochdwy's at Llandough is one of the oldest Christian sites in Wales, the seat of an early monastery. Beside it, on the slope above the river, stands the place that will become Tŷ Mawr: the Great House. This is a story about who owns that ground, and how the answer was buried.

> Title move — Great House (one farm): Church land, Llandough

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Wiki page: Master Timeline — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/

### P.2 (2). 12th – 14th century — An old house

Prologue: The Root · Scene id: ghf-12000101-1 · Date: 1200-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Archaeological record

In the Middle Ages people live and work on this slope; their pottery is still in the ground eight hundred years later. The house that grows here is old and grand: a long stone house the Royal Commission will judge sub-medieval, probably of the seventeenth century, perhaps built around something older still.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### P.3 (3). 1552 – 1829 — Cydfin, or Tŷ Mawr

Prologue: The Root · Scene id: ghf-15520101-1 · Date: 1552-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Estate papers

In the manor's leases it goes by an older name: Cydfin, or Tŷ Mawr, a farm of a hundred and seven acres. Every lease is written, signed and kept. Remember that. For three centuries this land's paper trail is unbroken.

> Title move — Great House (one farm): Manor of Llandough: Cydfin or Tŷ Mawr, 107 acres, on written leases

- Estate papers: National Library of Wales, Bute Estate Records D 219: Llandough manorial leases and agreements, 1552–1829 — https://archives.library.wales/index.php/llandough-manorial-leases-and-agreements
- Wiki page: Name & Location Variations — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/great-house-farm/name-variations/

### P.4 (4). Mid 16th – late 18th century — The Vaughans of Great House

Prologue: The Root · Scene id: ghf-15600101-1 · Date: 1560-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Heritage record

The title has a root. A letter to the Western Mail will one day trace it from Tewkesbury Abbey to the Crown and the Herberts. From the middle of the sixteenth century the Vaughans, a minor gentry family, hold Great House as the chief freehold farm of the parish. Their memorials are still in the church next door.

> Title move — Great House (one farm): Freehold: the Vaughans (root traced via Tewkesbury Abbey, the Crown and the Herberts)

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Newspaper: Western Mail, 'Grievous loss' (letter tracing the descent) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n04

### P.5 (5). 1667 — The Williamses arrive

Prologue: The Root · Scene id: ghf-16670101-1 · Date: 1667-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Mary's statement

In 1667 the Williams family come to Great House. Mary Williams, born there two and a half centuries later, will say her ancestors bought it. From now on, for more than three hundred years, there is a Williams in the house.

> Title move — Great House (one farm): Freehold: the Vaughans · in the house: the Williamses

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — origins — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### P.6 (6). Early 19th century — The Marquesses of Bute

Prologue: The Root · Scene id: ghf-18000101-1 · Date: 1800-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Heritage record

Early in the nineteenth century the Bute Estate, the greatest landowner in South Wales, takes the freehold. The manor courts of Llandough and Leckwith sit in the house itself. By 1818 Llandough's rents are in Bute's books, and in 1824 the estate's surveyor walks the farm and writes it down. One owner, one farm, one title.

> Title move — Great House (one farm): Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenants: the Williamses

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Wiki page: The Bute Estate — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bute-estate/
- Estate papers: National Library of Wales, Bute Estate Records R1: Glamorgan Estate rentals — https://archives.library.wales/index.php/glamorgan-estate-rentals
- Wiki page: Name & Location Variations (Stewart survey, D/d B E/1–2) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/great-house-farm/name-variations/

### P.7 (7). c. 1840 — The Great House shrinks

Prologue: The Root · Scene id: ghf-18400101-1 · Date: 1840-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Public record

Then, on paper, the Great House begins to shrink. In the census and the tithe returns it stops being 'Great House' and becomes 'Great House Farm': no longer the court house of a manor, just a farmhouse. It is the first time the records describe the place as something less than it is. In this story, how a thing is described will matter as much as what it is.

- Wiki page: Farmhouse Nomenclature — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/great-house-farm/farmhouse-nomenclature/
- Wiki page: Name & Location Variations — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/great-house-farm/name-variations/

### I.1 (8). c. 1858 — Bones by the church

Act I: The Split · Scene id: ghf-18580101-1 · Date: 1858-01-01 · Parcel: Not Great House Farm land · Basis: Museum record

Workmen digging foundations beside the church find six skeletons, a medieval spearhead and a spur. The bones are put back in the ground by the churchyard stile. Llandough's dead lie close under the surface. Nobody yet asks how many there are.

- Museum record: 1931 letter, Museum Wales file 63.24 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/ghf-e106-r33-a1-1931-letter-museum-wales-file-63-24/
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### I.2 (9). c. 1870 — The soldier under the floor

Act I: The Split · Scene id: ghf-18700101-1 · Date: 1870-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

Under the dining-room floor of the Great House, the family will always say, lies a soldier in armour, with his horse, his lance and a small shield. The story is told for a hundred years. It reaches the Daily Telegraph and the Royal Commission's files. Nobody ever lifts the floor to look.

- Newspaper: Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974 (dates the find to "about 1870") — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n03
- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### I.3 (10). 1876 – c. 1912 — The quarrymen

Act I: The Split · Scene id: ghf-18760101-1 · Date: 1876-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Estate papers

Limestone brings the quarrymen. The Bute Estate lets about thirty-three acres of the farm to the Llandough Limeworks, and for the next thirty-five years the quarry eats into the land.

- Wiki page: Llandough Limeworks — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/llandough-limeworks/

### I.4 (11). 1877 — The split

Act I: The Split · Scene id: ghf-18770101-1 · Date: 1877-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Mary's statement

1877. The move that everything turns on. The Bute Estate sells the farmhouse, its buildings and about ten acres to the quarryman Daniel Thomas. Call it Parcel A. Bute keeps nine acres of fields on the top. Call that Parcel B. From today they are two pieces of land with two owners and two chains of title. The Williamses stay on as tenants of both: of the house under Thomas, of the fields under Bute. And, as Mary will tell it, with a promise: when the quarrying ends, the freehold of the house comes to them. Hold on to this. Bute no longer owns the house. Anything Bute sells after today can only be Parcel B.

> The words: sold to Daniel Thomas … retained by the Bute Estate — Mary's account of the split: Parcel A (house and about 10 acres) to Thomas, Parcel B (about 9 acres on the top) kept by Bute.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold: Daniel Thomas (bought from Bute) · tenants: the Williamses, promised the freehold when quarrying ends
> Title move — Parcel B: the fields: Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenants: the Williamses

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — the sale — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#sale-1877
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — plan — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#plan
- Wiki page: The Two Parcels — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/the-two-parcels/
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — Bute lease — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#sale-1877

### I.5 (12). 11 November 1891 — Three geese

Act I: The Split · Scene id: ghf-18911111-1 · Date: 1891-11-11 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Newspaper

Fourteen years later three geese are stolen from "Mr. John Williams, Great House Farm, Llandough". The thief goes to court, and the newspaper records, in passing, who lives at the house.

- Newspaper: 1891 court report — farmyard theft — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n01

### I.6 (13). May 1897 — Marconi

Act I: The Split · Scene id: ghf-18970501-1 · Date: 1897-05-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Family account

In May 1897 Marconi sends the first wireless signals across open sea, from Lavernock Point to Flat Holm. In the family's memory it is Thomas Williams of Great House who carts his equipment down to the point.

- Newspaper: Press report of the Lavernock trials, 1897 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n02

### I.7 (14). 1908 — Two landlords

Act I: The Split · Scene id: ghf-19080101-1 · Date: 1908-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Mary's statement

Mary's grandfather dies, and her father, John Williams, takes over both tenancies: the house from the Thomases, the fields from Bute. Two parcels, two landlords, one family farming them as one. On the ground it looks like one farm. On paper it is two.

> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold: the Thomases · tenant: John Williams
> Title move — Parcel B: the fields: Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenant: John Williams

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: John Williams — 1908 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/john-williams/#y1908
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration (1905 Bute conveyance) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration

### I.8 (15). 10 August 1913 — Mary is born

Act I: The Split · Scene id: ghf-19130810-1 · Date: 1913-08-10 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Mary's statement

On 10 August 1913 Mary Williams is born in the farmhouse. She will live in it for the rest of her life, and she will die in it.

- Wiki page: Mary Williams — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams/
- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/

### II.1 (16). February 1916 — "The whole farm"

Act II: Two Words · Scene id: ghf-19160201-1 · Date: 1916-02-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Court record

February 1916. Bute lets John Williams "the whole farm" on a yearly tenancy. Read those words with what we now know. Bute has not owned the house since 1877. It owns the fields, Parcel B, and nothing else here. So "the whole farm" is a landlord describing land it does not own as if it did. The words are Bute's, not the family's. The tenancy itself has never been found; only those three words survive, quoted seventy years later by the Court of Appeal as the start of the story. From here on there are two Great House Farms: the real one, in two parcels, and a mythical one, a single estate that exists only on paper. Call it the synthetic farm. Every case against the family will be fought over the synthetic farm.

> The words: "the whole farm" — Both parcels, described as one by a landlord (Bute) that by then owned only Parcel B. The birth of the synthetic farm.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Seed (a landlord's wording, not the family's): the words "the whole farm" in a Bute tenancy (Bute can only let Parcel B)

- Court record: The 1916 Tenancy — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1916-tenancy/#grant
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Wiki page: The Farm / Whole Farm Nomenclature — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/the-two-parcels/whole-farm-nomenclature/

### II.2 (17). 1928 — The last rent

Act II: Two Words · Scene id: ghf-19280101-1 · Date: 1928-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Mary's statement

In 1928 the last of the quarry machinery leaves. John Williams pays a final rent of about four pounds to Alfred Thomas, and the bargain of 1877 comes due: the quarrying is over, and the freehold of the house passes to the family. Mary sees the receipt. From this year the true Parcel A has a complete chain: the Vaughans, Bute, Daniel Thomas, the Williamses. The family pay no more rent on the house, to anyone, ever again.

> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold: the Williamses (Bute → Thomas → Williams; 1877 agreement and 1928 receipt kept at the house)

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — takes effect 1928 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#takes-effect
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration (15 May 1924 agreement) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration

### II.3 (18). 1936 — Mary marries Frederick

Act II: Two Words · Scene id: ghf-19360101-1 · Date: 1936-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

Mary marries Frederick Buckler, a farmer, and he comes to live with her in the house. They will have seven children; the first, a son, is born within a few years. Note who owns what: the house is Mary's family's. Frederick will farm the fields.

- Wiki page: Frederick Buckler — marriage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#marriage
- Wiki page: Frederick Buckler — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/
- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### II.4 (19). 1938 — Bute sells out

Act II: Two Words · Scene id: ghf-19380101-1 · Date: 1938-01-01 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Court record

In 1938 Bute sells its interest to a property company, Western Ground Rents. The deed passes Bute's "reversion": its interest as landlord of the land it still owns and lets. That is Parcel B, the fields. It cannot include Parcel A; Bute sold that sixty years ago. So Western Ground Rents buys two things: the fields, and the habit of calling them "the whole farm". It has no deed to the house, and it never will.

> The words: Bute's "reversion" — Bute's interest as landlord of what it still owned and let: Parcel B. It could not include Parcel A.
> Title move — Parcel B: the fields: Freehold: Western Ground Rents (from Bute, 1938) · tenant: John Williams

- Wiki page: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1939-revised-tenancy/#y1938
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

### II.5 (20). May 1939 — The plan

Act II: Two Words · Scene id: ghf-19390501-1 · Date: 1939-05-01 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Document

A year later Western Ground Rents gives John Williams a new tenancy, with a plan. The plan shows the fields east of the house. The house is not on it. The new landlord's own document draws the line of 1877: its tenancy is of Parcel B, and only Parcel B. It is the last written tenancy there will ever be.

> The words: the tenancy plan — The fields east of the house: Parcel B only. The landlord's own document leaves the house out.
> Title move — Parcel B: the fields: Freehold: Western Ground Rents · tenant: John Williams (1939 plan: fields only)

- Wiki page: 1938–39: the 1939 tenancy — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1939-revised-tenancy/#y1939
- Wiki page: The 1939 tenancy plan — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1939-revised-tenancy/#plan

### II.6 (21). c. 1940 — Twelve years

Act II: Two Words · Scene id: ghf-19400101-1 · Date: 1940-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family case

By 1940 the Williamses, John and his daughter Mary in the house, have lived there twelve years without paying anyone a penny for it. In law, twelve years is enough. So from 1940 the family hold Parcel A twice over: by the bargain of 1877, and by time. Even without a single paper, there is from now on no basis for anyone to call Mary's occupation of her house permissive. Everything that follows has to pretend this year never happened.

> The words: twelve years, rent-free — Title by possession to Parcel A, complete by 1940, on top of the 1877–1928 bargain.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold: the Williamses, by the 1877 bargain and by title by possession (twelve years rent-free, 1928–1940)

- Wiki page: 1938–39 — c. 1940 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1939-revised-tenancy/#c1940

### II.7 (22). 1944 — War on the land

Act II: Two Words · Scene id: ghf-19440101-1 · Date: 1944-01-01 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Mary's statement

The war is on, the farm is struggling, and the War Agricultural Committee wants it run better. Frederick takes over the fields as manager for his father-in-law.

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: John Williams — 1944 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/john-williams/#y1944

### II.8 (23). c. 1948 – 49 — Billy is born

Act II: Two Words · Scene id: ghf-19480101-1 · Date: 1948-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

William Buckler, Billy, is born at the farm. He will be the last of the family to live there, and the one they evict.

- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — William — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### III.1 (24). 2 February 1949 — Nothing in writing

Act III: The Mimic · Scene id: ghf-19490202-1 · Date: 1949-02-02 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Court record

February 1949. John Williams gives up his tenancy of the fields, and Frederick takes them on from Western Ground Rents. Nothing is written down: no lease, no plan. And now the first attempt to make Mary's occupation look permissive: the landlord begins to speak of Frederick's fields tenancy as a tenancy of "the farm", house and all, as if the house were his and she lived there by his tenancy. Mary rejects it. The house is hers, it was never in any tenancy of the fields, and she has the paper title in the blanket box to prove it. Note who blurs the two parcels here. Not the family. The landlord's own 1939 plan shows it knew exactly where the line was.

> The words: "the farm" (Frederick's tenancy) — Never written down. On the facts, the fields: Parcel B. Speaking of it as the farm, house and all, is the first attempt to make Mary look permitted.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Attempt 1 to make Mary look permitted: her house spoken of as part of Frederick's unwritten fields tenancy (Mary rejects it; she still holds the paper title)
> Title move — Parcel B: the fields: Freehold: Western Ground Rents · tenant: Frederick Buckler (unwritten, from 1949)

- Court record: Frederick Buckler — the 1949 tenancy — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#tenancy-1949
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Wiki page: The Two Parcels — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/the-two-parcels/

### III.2 (25). June 1950 – c. 1952 — The blanket box

Act III: The Mimic · Scene id: ghf-19500601-1 · Date: 1950-06-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Mary's statement

1950. An estate agent from Penarth places a lodger in the farmhouse. He stays two years. Before he goes, he tells Mary what he has done: he has taken the papers from the family's blanket box, 'including the agreement relating to the farm', and handed them to the agent. Mary will say she believed it was connected with the landlord's first move against the farm, which comes within three years. Think about what it means. The true Parcel A still exists, and its chain is still complete. But the paper that proves it has left the house a year after she produced it as her answer. From now on, every time Mary says 'the house is mine', she will be asked for documents she no longer has.

> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold: the Williamses · their deeds taken from the blanket box (missing from now on; title buried, not extinguished)

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — papers taken — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#papers-taken

### III.3 (26). 1952 – 53 — The last rent on the fields

Act III: The Mimic · Scene id: ghf-19521010-1 · Date: 1952-10-10 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Court record

In October 1952 the landlord's agents write that they will not go on with a letting to Frederick. He pays his last rent on the fields the next year. After that the family pay no one for anything.

- Court record: Frederick Buckler — 1952 letter — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#tenancy-1949
- Wiki page: Master Timeline — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/

### III.4 (27). 2 February 1955 — The first order

Act III: The Mimic · Scene id: ghf-19550202-1 · Date: 1955-02-02 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Court record

February 1955. Western Ground Rents sues Frederick, its tenant of the fields, and gets a High Court order for possession of "the whole of the farm". Now unpack it. The tenancy that ended was a tenancy of the fields. The landlord was the owner of the fields. An order giving a landlord back what it let can only reach Parcel B. "The whole of the farm" is the synthetic farm again: borrowed words that reach over the house without the landlord ever proving a right to it. Mary, who owns the house, is not a party and is never heard. On 4 July the order is enforced. The fields are taken. The family's account is that the woodland on the north side of Parcel A goes too, to a couple in Llandough, and later to a charity that has never touched it. The house is left: Mary, just home from hospital after losing a leg, stands her ground. Years later this order will be read as the day a twelve-year clock started running on her house. It wasn't. Whatever clock started in 1955 was a clock on the fields. The second attempt to make Mary's occupation look permissive is an insinuation, and it will later be mistaken for a fact.

> The words: "the whole of the farm" — As a matter of law, only what the landlord let and owned: Parcel B. As enforced on 4 July 1955: the fields (and, on the family's account, the woodland). Not the house.
> The words: adverse possession "from 1955" — The clock the 1987 court counted. It can only have been a clock on the fields; Parcel A was never Western Ground Rents's.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · woodland half of Parcel A taken in 1955 (family account)
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Attempt 2: High Court order against the fields tenant for "the whole of the farm" (house not taken; Mary never heard)
> Title move — Parcel B: the fields: Freehold and possession: Western Ground Rents (fields taken 4 July 1955)

- Court record: The 1955 Possession Order — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1955-possession-order/#order
- Court record: The 1955 Possession Order — enforcement — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1955-possession-order/#enforcement

### III.5 (28). 1959 — Mary says no

Act III: The Mimic · Scene id: ghf-19590101-1 · Date: 1959-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

The third attempt. In 1959 Western Ground Rents offers Mary a tenancy of "the farmhouse and garden", on their own. Notice the words. Not "the farm" this time. The landlord names the house parcel by itself: Parcel A, less the woodland to the north and the land to the south already being taken from around it. It knows exactly which piece is separate, and exactly which piece it has no deed to. Why else offer a tenancy of a house you say you own? If she signs, she becomes a tenant, and a tenant's occupation is permissive by definition. She refuses. The house is hers, she tells them, through her grandfather, and there are documents to prove it. The documents are in someone else's hands. The court will one day record that they were "never produced".

> The words: "the farmhouse and garden" — Parcel A (the farmhouse, yard and garden), less the woodland to the north and the land to the south already taken. The landlord now names the house parcel on its own.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Attempt 3: tenancy of her own farmhouse and garden offered to Mary (refused)

- Court record: The 1962 Possession Order — 1959 refusal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#refusal-1959
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

### III.6 (29). 11 December 1962 — The 1962 order

Act III: The Mimic · Scene id: ghf-19621211-1 · Date: 1962-12-11 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

The fourth attempt, and the one that will matter most. 11 December 1962: in Cardiff County Court, Judge Temple Morris QC orders Frederick and Mary out of "the farmhouse and garden", and to pay for every year back to 1955. Again the house parcel, named on its own. For the first time Mary is a party. But this is a possession order, not a ruling on title. It treats her as someone holding over on the old "whole farm" tenancy, a permitted occupier who has outstayed her welcome, when she was never in that tenancy at all. Western Ground Rents proves no deed to the house, because it has none. And then it does nothing. The order is never carried out. It goes into a drawer. Twenty-five years from now, it is what will save BP's case.

> The words: "the farmhouse and garden" — Parcel A (the farmhouse, yard and garden), less the woodland to the north and the land to the south already taken, ordered back as if held over from a tenancy it was never in.
> The words: possession order — Who may occupy, not who owns. No deed to the house was proved.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Attempt 4: county court possession order for the farmhouse and garden, treating Mary as holding over (no deed proven; never enforced)

- Court record: The 1962 Possession Order — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#order
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration (29 March 1961 deed) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration

### III.7 (30). June 1963 — Committal

Act III: The Mimic · Scene id: ghf-19630601-1 · Date: 1963-06-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

The landlord goes after Frederick for the money under the order, and committal proceedings follow. Possession is not taken. The money, not the house, is enforced. The threat of prison now hangs over the family for staying in their own home.

- Court record: The 1962 Possession Order — committal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#committal
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### III.8 (31). January – March 1965 — Two pounds a week

Act III: The Mimic · Scene id: ghf-19650301-1 · Date: 1965-03-02 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Document

The fifth attempt. 2 March 1965: the agents offer 'Mrs Williams' a weekly tenancy of the farmhouse and garden at two pounds a week. The same trap as 1959: sign, and the owner becomes a tenant. Mary does not sign it, does not send it back, and does not pay. Even the landlord's own records now count her occupation as adverse: hers, not theirs. Step back and look at the pattern. An owner who holds the deed to a house does not need to fold it into someone else's tenancy, word an order against the wrong tenant, offer the occupier a tenancy, then another. An owner sues on its deed. Western Ground Rents never once did.

> The words: weekly tenancy to "Mrs Williams" — An offer that only makes sense if the offeror needed her to become a tenant. Not signed; her occupation treated as adverse from then.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Attempt 5: weekly tenancy offered to "Mrs Williams" (not signed; her occupation now treated as adverse)

- Wiki page: The 1965 offer — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#offer-1965
- Wiki page: Mary Williams — 1965 offer — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams/#chronology

### III.9 (32). 1964 – 68 — A rumoured sale

Act III: The Mimic · Scene id: ghf-19640101-1 · Date: 1965-06-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Family account

Somewhere in these years, a cousin will later say, the eldest son sells "our land parcel" through a solicitor, behind his parents' backs. What he sold, and to whom, has never come to light. In 1968 he and his household leave the farm.

- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — rumoured sale — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/
- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### III.10 (33). 1967 — Frederick dies

Act III: The Mimic · Scene id: ghf-19670101-1 · Date: 1967-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

Frederick Buckler dies at fifty-six. With him goes the only tenant there ever was. Mary takes back her maiden name, Williams, and stays on in the house she was born in: an owner who has never been a tenant.

> Title move — Parcel B: the fields: Freehold and possession: Western Ground Rents

- Wiki page: Frederick Buckler — death — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#death

### IV.1 (34). 31 December 1969 — The handover

Act IV: The Handover · Scene id: ghf-19691231-1 · Date: 1969-12-31 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

31 December 1969. Western Ground Rents sells out to the BP Pension Trust, the pension fund of British Petroleum. The conveyance speaks of "Great House Farm", one estate: the synthetic farm passes one more time in a single phrase. Look at what can actually pass. Parcel B, the fields, passes with a proper chain: Bute, Western Ground Rents, BP. For the house, Western Ground Rents has no deed to hand over. What it has is a case: the 1962 order, the refused tenancies, the "whole farm" wording. That is what BP takes on for Parcel A: not the house, but the claim against it. This conveyance will later be recited as the root of BP's title. Today it is missing from the Land Registry's files.

> The words: "Great House Farm" — The synthetic farm in one phrase. By deed: Parcel B. For Parcel A: only the 1962 order and the case against Mary. The deed itself is now missing.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Held by BP Pension Trust: the 1962 order and the case against Mary (no deed to Parcel A; the 1969 root conveyance now missing)
> Title move — Parcel B: the fields: Freehold: BP Pension Trust (Bute → WGR → BP, by deed)

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — conveyances — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#conveyances

### IV.2 (35). 1970 – 72 — Plans drawn around her

Act IV: The Handover · Scene id: ghf-19720725-1 · Date: 1972-07-25 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

Around Mary, the plans are already being drawn. The council takes the land south of her farmhouse, part of Parcel A, and in 1970 it is registered as village green VG41; by the 1980s it is laid out as a green. In July 1972 planning permission is granted for houses on the site, with Mary still living in the middle of it. Piece by piece, Parcel A is being taken from around her. The development needs the house. The house needs a title.

> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · woodland taken 1955 · land south of the farmhouse taken by the council: village green VG41 (1970)

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Wiki page: Master Timeline — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/

### IV.3 (36). 1974 — Half a survey

Act IV: The Handover · Scene id: ghf-19740101-1 · Date: 1974-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Heritage record

The Royal Commission sends a surveyor to record the old house. He gets as far as the ground floor. The rest, he notes, cannot be examined 'because of problems of access created by an ownership dispute'. A public body writes it down in 1974: the ownership of this house is disputed.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### IV.4 (37). 15 April 1974 — Open day

Act IV: The Handover · Scene id: ghf-19740415-1 · Date: 1974-04-15 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 15 April 1974 Mary, now sixty, opens her home to the public 'to show what the nation is losing'. Hundreds come, and a thousand sign a petition. She tells the Daily Telegraph that ownership of the house has been disputed for twenty-five years, that she will refuse to move, and that her solicitors say she has a valid claim. It is in a national newspaper: she claims to own the house.

- Newspaper: Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974, 'Open day to save ancient Welsh house' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n03
- Wiki page: The 1974 Licence Letters — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#action

### IV.5 (38). 3 July 1974 — Mary pleads ownership

Act IV: The Handover · Scene id: ghf-19740703-1 · Date: 1974-07-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

BP Pension Trust brings a new county court action for possession of the house. On 3 July 1974 Mary does what nobody has yet let her do: in court, in her defence, she pleads that the house is hers, and the Limitation Act besides. Her statement tells the history in her own words: the farmhouse, buildings and about ten acres sold by Bute to Daniel Thomas; about nine acres on the top kept by Bute. The two parcels, from the woman who lived on one of them. Now the question of title is finally before a judge. The hearing is part heard and adjourned, and BP never brings it back. Her claim to own the house is never decided, then or ever. It is never extinguished. And no lawyer of hers ever builds the case her statement contains.

> The words: ownership and the Limitation Act — Mary's plea of title to Parcel A, in court. Adjourned and never decided, so never extinguished.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claimed by Mary, in occupation · ownership pleaded in court, 3 July 1974 (adjourned, never decided)

- Court record: The 1974 Licence Letters — the action — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#action
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

### IV.6 (39). September – October 1974 — The licence letters

Act IV: The Handover · Scene id: ghf-19741031-1 · Date: 1974-10-31 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

The sixth attempt, and the one that works. Instead of fighting the title case it started, BP reaches back for the old 1962 order. On 19 September it gets leave to enforce it; Mary is given no notice. Then, on 31 October, BP withdraws the warrant and writes to her instead, 'licensing' her to stay in the farmhouse rent-free for the rest of her life. Why would an owner need a licence? She doesn't, and she never accepts it. But a licence does not need to be accepted to be useful. On paper, from today, BP can say she lives there with its permission. A tenancy refused, a tenancy refused, an order never enforced, and now a licence nobody asked for: sequence, stealth, force and licence. It is how you build permission when you have no deed. BP keeps the letters.

> The words: "licence" — Permission offered to an owner who never asked for it and never accepted it. The sixth attempt, and the one the courts relied on.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Attempt 6: BP's "licence" letters to Mary, 31 October 1974 (never accepted); 1962 warrant withdrawn

- Court record: The 1974 Licence Letters — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#letters
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Court record: The 1974 Licence Letters — the warrant — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#warrant

### IV.7 (40). 19 November, 1970s (year unclear) — "Grievous loss"

Act IV: The Handover · Scene id: ghf-19741119-1 · Date: 1974-11-19 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

A letter to the Western Mail warns that pulling down Great House would wipe out the site of St Dochdwy's Celtic monastery, and traces the land back through Tewkesbury Abbey, the Crown, the Herberts and Bute. The true chain of title is printed in a newspaper. Nobody follows it.

- Newspaper: Western Mail, 'Grievous loss' (letter) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n04
- Wiki page: The Restoration Campaign — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/restoration-campaign/#open-day-1974

### IV.8 (41). 23 May 1975 — A deed for the mimic

Act IV: The Handover · Scene id: ghf-19750523-1 · Date: 1975-05-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

Now the paper. 23 May 1975: the BP Pension Trust conveys "the farmhouse and garden" to its sister company, BP Properties, with a plan. The Court of Appeal will later call it "the actual conveyance of the farmhouse and garden". Stop there. One BP company conveys Mary's house to another while she lives in it and claims it in court. The seller has no deed to the house from Bute, from the Thomases, or from anyone. And this is the plainest proof that BP knew the house was a separate piece of land: it needed a separate deed for it. After today the synthetic Parcel A has something it never had before, a conveyance of its own.

> The words: "the actual conveyance of the farmhouse and garden" — Parcel A, conveyed from one BP company to another, with no earlier deed to it behind it. Proof BP treated the house as a separate piece of land.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Paper: conveyance BP Pension Trust → BP Properties of "the farmhouse and garden" (no earlier deed to Parcel A behind it)

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — conveyances — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#conveyances

### IV.9 (42). 22 May 1980 — "The most rapacious ground landlord"

Act IV: The Handover · Scene id: ghf-19800522-1 · Date: 1980-05-22 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Parliament

In May 1980 Ted Rowlands MP tells the House of Commons that Western Ground Rents, 'the most rapacious ground landlord' in South Wales, has been bought by the BP pension fund. The company that built the case against the house in the 1950s and 60s, and the company that inherited it, are now one family.

- Newspaper: Hansard, 22 May 1980 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n16

### IV.10 (43). 1 October 1982 — A warning about the ground

Act IV: The Handover · Scene id: ghf-19821001-1 · Date: 1982-10-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

In October 1982 GGAT, the regional archaeological trust, warns the planners that the ancient settlement may run north of the church, under the farm, and asks for thorough investigation before anything is built.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/
- Newspaper: Neath Guardian, 17 April 1980 (Roman villa, a separate site) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n05
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 18 March 1983 — burnt relics (Roman villa finds, a separate site) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n06

### IV.11 (44). 19 – 30 November 1982 — First registration: the fields

Act IV: The Handover · Scene id: ghf-19821119-1 · Date: 1982-11-19 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

November 1982: BP's solicitors apply to register the land at HM Land Registry for the first time, as one main title. Once land is registered, the register is the title. Mary is seventy and living in the farmhouse. Nothing on the file shows anyone asking her what she claims.

> The words: first registration — BP's main title. On paper Parcel B (the fields).
> Title move — Parcel B: the fields: Registered: BP Properties, main title WA231076 (applied 30 November 1982)

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — first registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Analysis: 1982–83 Registration & Opportunity to Object — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/procedural-fairness-notice/1982-83-registration-opportunity-to-object/

### IV.12 (45). 23 February 1983 — First registration: the mimic

Act IV: The Handover · Scene id: ghf-19830223-1 · Date: 1983-02-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

February 1983: a second application, for "the farmhouse and garden" as a separate title, resting on the 1975 conveyance between the two BP companies. The solicitors certify that they know of "no question or doubt" affecting the title. The woman who pleaded ownership in court nine years ago is living in the house. Now the Land Registry holds, in its own files, the fields under one number and the house under another. It knows they are two. And the synthetic Parcel A is no longer just a conveyance. It is a registered title, issued by the state.

> The words: "the farmhouse and garden" as a separate title — The synthetic Parcel A, registered on the 1975 BP-to-BP conveyance.
> The words: "no question or doubt" — Certified while the owner who had pleaded ownership in 1974 lived in the house.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Paper: registered as a separate title, WA240304, on the 1975 conveyance ("no question or doubt")

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — first registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### IV.13 (46). 26 March 1983 — Mary dies

Act IV: The Handover · Scene id: ghf-19830326-1 · Date: 1983-03-26 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

On 26 March 1983, a month later, Mary Williams dies in the farmhouse where she was born. She dies an owner who never signed a tenancy and never accepted a licence, with her claim never decided. Her son Billy inherits it, and the house, and the fight.

> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim passes to Billy Buckler, in occupation · never decided, never extinguished

- Wiki page: Mary Williams — death — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams/#death
- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — William — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### IV.14 (47). 8 April – 12 May 1983 — Letters after her death

Act IV: The Handover · Scene id: ghf-19830408-1 · Date: 1983-04-08 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

Two weeks after Mary's death, BP's solicitors and the Land Registry are writing to each other about the farmhouse file, including an 'inside examination' form. What the Registry asked about the family living in the house, and what it was told, is in those letters.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — first registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration

### V.1 (48). 1984 — BP's writ

Act V: Possession, Not Ownership · Scene id: ghf-19840522-1 · Date: 1984-05-22 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

May 1984. BP Properties serves Billy with a writ for possession of "Great House Farm and adjoining land". The synthetic farm again: the house wrapped back inside "the farm", a year after BP registered it as a separate title. BP does not ask the court to declare that it owns the house. It asks only for possession. And Billy's side answers on BP's terms: adverse possession, twelve years counted from 1955. Think about what that concedes. Adverse to whom? To the owners of "the farm". But their only real title was to the fields. The family end up claiming adverse possession of a mythical estate, with the clock started by an order about Parcel B, when their own title to Parcel A was complete by 1928 and secured by possession by 1940. Mary's own case, the 1877 split, is never run. That same year, the family learn, the library's copy of the 1877 deed goes missing.

> The words: "Great House Farm and adjoining land" — The house wrapped back into the synthetic farm, a year after BP registered it separately.
> The words: adverse possession from 1955 — The family's defence, fought on the other side's map: possession adverse to owners of "the farm", whose real title was only to Parcel B.
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — the writ — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#writ
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — library copy missing — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#library-1984
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration

### V.2 (49). 10 July 1986 — Judgment for BP

Act V: Possession, Not Ownership · Scene id: ghf-19860710-1 · Date: 1986-07-10 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

10 July 1986, the High Court at Cardiff. Mr Justice Hollis finds for BP: the 1974 letters gave Mary a licence, so her possession was never adverse. The sixth attempt has done its work. Both sides have argued about the synthetic farm. Nobody has argued about Parcel A. The deed of 1877, the receipt of 1928, the 1939 plan that left the house out: none of it is before the judge. The question of who owns the house is never put.

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — High Court — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#high-court
- Analysis: BP v Buckler: Scope, Decided & Undecided — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/court-judicial-issues/bp-v-buckler-scope-decided-undecided/

### V.3 (50). 1986 – 87 — A file goes missing

Act V: Possession, Not Ownership · Scene id: ghf-19860711-1 · Date: 1986-07-11 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

While the case goes on, the Royal Commission's correspondence with Mrs Buckler goes missing from its files: letters in which she may have told an independent public body, in her own words, why the house was hers.

- Analysis: Legal Review — the loss pattern — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/#loss-pattern

### V.4 (51). 2 February 1987 — The merger

Act V: Possession, Not Ownership · Scene id: ghf-19870202-1 · Date: 1987-02-02 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

2 February 1987, with Billy's appeal still waiting to be heard: an application to fold the farmhouse title into the main title for the fields. Here is the proof that they knew. You cannot merge two titles unless there are two. Since 1983 BP and the Land Registry have held the house and the fields as separate titles, while the case was argued in court as if they had always been one farm. The merger makes the fiction true on paper, in the middle of the appeal. From now on there is no separate record of the house to examine, no line on the register where its missing root could be noticed. The synthetic Parcel A disappears into Parcel B. The true Parcel A is still there, underneath. It has never been extinguished. It has been buried.

> The words: amalgamation — Two titles joined into one: the synthetic Parcel A folded into Parcel B. Proof that both BP and the Registry knew they were two.
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": Registered: BP Properties, WA231076 = Parcel B + synthetic Parcel A (farmhouse title folded in, 2 February 1987)

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — amalgamation — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Analysis: 1987 HMLR Amalgamation During Appeal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/procedural-fairness-notice/1987-hmlr-amalgamation-during-appeal/

### V.5 (52). 31 July 1987 — The Court of Appeal

Act V: Possession, Not Ownership · Scene id: ghf-19870731-1 · Date: 1987-07-31 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

31 July 1987, the Court of Appeal. Here is the twist. The judges find that Frederick and Mary were in adverse possession of the house from 1955. The clock was running against the landlord. So why does BP win? Because of two of the attempts. The 1962 order, never enforced, was brought within twelve years and so stopped the clock. And the 1974 letters made Mary's possession permissive, the court holds, whether she accepted them or not. Now look at what is in front of the judges. A conveyance they themselves call "the actual conveyance of the farmhouse and garden": a separate deed for the house. Yet the case is decided as one farm, with the clock started in 1955 by an order about the fields. Count from 1928, as the house's own history requires, and the twelve years were up in 1940, fifteen years before any order. Mary's title documents, the judgment notes, were "never produced". Nobody asks where they went. BP is recorded as having "the paper title to the farm": paper to the fields, and for the house only a deed between two BP companies. BP Properties Ltd v Buckler goes into the law books as a leading case on adverse possession. It decided possession. It never decided ownership.

> The words: "the paper title to the farm" — Paper to Parcel B; for Parcel A, only a deed between two BP companies.
> The words: "never produced" — Mary's title documents, taken from the blanket box in 1950–52.
> The words: adverse possession from 1955, stopped by the 1962 order and the 1974 licence — The clock was counted on the synthetic farm. On Parcel A it had run out in 1940.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Billy Buckler · never adjudicated, never extinguished (judgment decides possession only)
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": WA231076, BP Properties · right to possession upheld (1962 order + 1974 licence)

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Analysis: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — what it omits — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#omits

### V.6 (53). 3 March 1988 — Twenty-eight days

Act V: Possession, Not Ownership · Scene id: ghf-19880303-1 · Date: 1988-03-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 3 March 1988 the House of Lords refuses leave to appeal. The family are given twenty-eight days to leave a house the Williamses have lived in for three hundred years, on an order that never said whose house it was.

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — House of Lords — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#house-of-lords

### VI.1 (54). 29 April 1988, morning — The bailiffs come

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19880429-1 · Date: 1988-04-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

29 April 1988. Five bailiffs and fifteen police officers come up the lane. Billy blocks the narrow drive with a tractor, locks the doors and bars the windows.

- Newspaper: 'Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on', c. 30 April 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n07
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 29 April 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-01) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.2 (55). 29 April 1988 — The chainsaw

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19880429-2 · Date: 1988-04-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

The bailiffs smash the gate and take poleaxes to the doors. When an axe comes through a door with his three small children behind it, Billy starts a chainsaw and pushes it through. The bailiffs fall back. After four hours they leave. Branwen takes the children away. BP tells the press it let Mary stay out of kindness. Billy tells them the farm is theirs. Both are talking about the 1974 letters. Only one of them knows what they were for.

- Newspaper: 'Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n07
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 30 April 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-02) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.3 (56). May 1988 — "Someone will be killed"

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19880512-1 · Date: 1988-05-12 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Billy takes his case to the European Commission of Human Rights in Strasbourg. On 12 May the Cardiff MP Alun Michael asks the Lord Chancellor to look at it again. Billy warns that someone is going to be killed.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 12 May 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-03) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — ECHR — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#echr

### VI.4 (57). 29 July 1988 — Cadw comes to look

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19880729-1 · Date: 1988-07-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Photograph

On 29 July Cadw, the Welsh heritage body, comes to look at the house for listing, and photographs the farmhouse and the barn. Listing would protect the building, whoever owned it. Those two photographs are all that is left of the visit. No notes, no file, no record of who decided.

- Photograph: Cadw survey photograph of the farmhouse, 29 July 1988 (released 2026, ATISN 27021) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/foi-reply-register/#R37
- Photograph: Cadw survey photograph of the barn, 29 July 1988 (released 2026, ATISN 27021) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/foi-reply-register/#R37
- Analysis: Cadw — Forensic Critique — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/cadw-forensic-critique-v8-0-0/

### VI.5 (58). 29 – 30 November 1988 — Forced entry

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881130-1 · Date: 1988-11-30 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

29 November. The bailiffs come back, and this time they force their way in. Within hours, the family say, the demolition has begun: half the roof is already off an outbuilding. Billy is taken to Llandough Hospital. Eight other people living at the farm lose their homes with the family. For the first time in three hundred years, there is no Williams in the house.

> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Billy Buckler, evicted 29 November 1988 · never adjudicated, never extinguished
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": WA231076, BP Properties · in possession from 29 November 1988

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo front page — 'Angry scenes as farmer evicted' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n14
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 30 November 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-04) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — 'Billy's unhappy family' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n09

### VI.6 (59). 1 December 1988 — Everything in the road

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881201-1 · Date: 1988-12-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Billy lies injured in hospital. Branwen and the children have nowhere to go. Mary's whole life, her photographs, the family heirlooms, the legal papers, is left in the house or thrown into the road. Billy has the clothes he stands in.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n08
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 13 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-11) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.7 (60). 2 December 1988 — Do not touch the house

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881202-1 · Date: 1988-12-02 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 2 December a High Court judge orders that the farmhouse and everything in it must not be touched. Branwen may go in for her belongings, if BP's solicitors agree. BP says it means to demolish and build new homes on the ten acres.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — 'History fight to save farm' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n08
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 2 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-05) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.8 (61). 3 December 1988 — From hospital bed to the dock

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881209-1 · Date: 1988-12-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Police take Billy from his hospital bed and charge him with assaulting two bailiffs, criminal damage, and furious driving.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-06) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n15

### VI.9 (62). 3 – 5 December 1988 — One weekend

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881203-1 · Date: 1988-12-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

Over one weekend, without setting foot inside, Cadw considers emergency listing. In public it says it is looking at the house. In July it had already marked it just below the bar.

- Analysis: Cadw — Forensic Critique — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/cadw-forensic-critique-v8-0-0/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — Cadw considering spot-listing — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n08

### VI.10 (63). Monday 5 December 1988 — Nothing more we can do

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881205-1 · Date: 1988-12-05 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Monday 5 December. Judge Norman Francis refuses to keep the injunction in place until Strasbourg can hear the family. Their solicitor says there is nothing more they can do. The same day Cadw announces that the house is not of sufficient merit to list. Nothing now protects it.

- Newspaper: Western Mail, 6 December 1988 — 'Farmer fails in final eviction hearing' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n10

### VI.11 (64). 6 December 1988, 4am — Bulldozed before breakfast

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881206-1 · Date: 1988-12-06 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

6 December 1988. Just after four in the morning, a twenty-strong team arrives with bulldozers. By breakfast no building is left standing. Branwen and the children watch their home go. The old court house of the manor, the soldier under the floor, the evidence of what the house was: gone before the day has begun. You can demolish a house. You cannot demolish a title. The true Parcel A is still there, under the rubble, undecided.

> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Billy Buckler · house demolished 6 December 1988 · title never adjudicated, never extinguished

- Newspaper: 'Tears flow as 800 year-old farm house is razed at last' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n11
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 6 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-07) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 21 December 1988 (reader's letter on "Bulldozed Before Breakfast") (search extract GHF-E090-N15-12) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s

### VI.12 (65). 7 – 9 December 1988 — Like a battlefield

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881208-1 · Date: 1988-12-07 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Llandough is furious. A county councillor, himself a BP pensioner, calls it 'disgusting'. Villagers confront their councillors. The council's planning chief, the family remember, says the site looks like a battlefield. On 9 December magistrates bail Billy on condition that he stays away from the land he was born on.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 7 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-08) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 9 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-09) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 10 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-10) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Wiki page: 1988: Possession and Demolition — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/demolition-1988/

### VI.13 (66). December 1988 — In the rubble

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881212-1 · Date: 1988-12-12 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Heritage record

In the rubble a Royal Commission investigator finds what the bulldozers left: a carved fireplace jamb, and a moulded beam of a kind rare in Glamorgan. And he records what is lost: a carved stone capital that stood by the front door, probably taken long ago from the old church.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### VII.1 (67). 20 March 1989 — Clearing the site

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19890320-1 · Date: 1989-03-20 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 20 March 1989, at half past seven in the morning, the lorries move in to carry away what is left.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 20 March 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-14) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VII.2 (68). January – March 1989 — "I will fight on"

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19890323-1 · Date: 1989-03-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

In January one charge is dropped as out of time, and Billy is told not to come within half a mile of the site. On 23 March he pleads guilty to the rest and walks free. He will fight on, he says, for his home and for more than seventy acres of land.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 23 March 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-15) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 24 March 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-16) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: 'Charge against evicted farmer dropped', January 1989 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n12
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 6 January 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-13) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VII.3 (69). 1989 — From farm to a bus

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19890325-1 · Date: 1989-03-25 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

The family who lived in the Great House now live with Billy's sister in Penarth. Billy plans to make a home in an old bus. Thirty thousand pounds' worth of his belongings, he says, were taken from the site after the demolition.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 1989 — 'From farm to a bus' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n13

### VII.4 (70). 14 April 1989 — Strasbourg says no

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19890414-1 · Date: 1989-04-14 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

In April 1989 Strasbourg rules. The European Commission accepts that the eviction interfered with Billy's home, but finds it lawful, to protect BP's rights as owner. It says Billy had no 'possession' in law, because the domestic courts had held the property belonged to another. But the domestic courts never held that. They decided possession. Strasbourg never saw a title deed either.

> The words: "the property belonged to another" — What Strasbourg understood the courts to have held. They had decided possession only.
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — ECHR — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#echr
- Court record: Buckler v United Kingdom, Commission decision (PDF) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/wp-1790112811838.pdf

### VII.5 (71). October – November 1989 — BP applies to build

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19891107-1 · Date: 1989-11-07 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

In November 1989 BP applies for permission to build houses on the farm. GGAT advises that nothing should be decided without an archaeological assessment. Then BP hires GGAT to do it. Their report calls the lost farmhouse 'a county treasure'.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings

### VII.6 (72). February – March 1990 — "Unfortunately demolished"

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19900313-1 · Date: 1990-03-13 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

In March 1990 outline permission is granted. The planning officer notes that the Local Plan said the farm buildings should be kept, 'however they were unfortunately demolished a little while ago'. No preservation notice was ever served. Part of the archaeologists' advice is missing from the file.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.7 (73). August – October 1990 — Eight trenches

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19900801-1 · Date: 1990-08-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

In August 1990 GGAT cuts eight trenches for BP. They find early medieval burials. A large area they could not investigate is marked as low potential, and in October the council signs the archaeology off.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/
- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/

### VII.8 (74). 21 August 1991 — The obituary

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19910821-1 · Date: 1991-08-21 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Heritage record

In 1991 the official heritage record writes the house's obituary. It 'was suddenly and completely demolished by B.P. Properties Ltd. on 6th December 1988 amid considerable local controversy'.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s

### VII.9 (75). 14 May 1992 — Twenty houses

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19920514-1 · Date: 1992-05-14 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

In May 1992 Ideal Homes applies to build twenty detached houses on the farm, on land BP has not yet transferred to it.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/

### VII.10 (76). 15 May 1992 — Billy dies

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19920515-1 · Date: 1992-05-15 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

The next day, 15 May 1992, Billy Buckler dies of a heart attack in Llandough Hospital, in the village where he was born. He is buried at Michaelston-le-Pit. He never gets his home back. His mother's claim passes, undecided, to his children.

> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Mary's heirs · never adjudicated, never extinguished

- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — William — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### VII.11 (77). 27 July 1992 — A warning, half missing

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19920727-1 · Date: 1992-07-27 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Planning file

In July 1992 GGAT warns the council that the ground holds significant remains, medieval and perhaps older, and human bone. Page two of the letter is missing from the file.

- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/

### VII.12 (78). 3 September 1992 — Approved anyway

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19920903-1 · Date: 1992-09-03 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

Thirty-eight days later the twenty houses are approved, with no new archaeological condition.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/

### VII.13 (79). December 1993 — The diggers move in

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19931203-1 · Date: 1993-12-03 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

In December 1993 BP transfers the merged title to Ideal Homes. The synthetic Parcel A now passes to a buyer as if it were the real thing, folded inside the fields. The diggers move in before the archaeology has been dealt with. GGAT asks the council to stop the work. The developer produces a barrister's opinion that the condition is met. The council accepts it: 'a difference of opinion', it later tells the MP.

> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": WA231076 transferred by BP to Ideal Homes (December 1993); later Persimmon Homes (Wales)

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.14 (80). March – July 1994 — A thousand graves

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19940504-1 · Date: 1994-03-21 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

In the spring of 1994 the excavators find what the trenches missed. Burial after burial lies just below the topsoil, in the ground the 1990 report called low potential. By the end there are more than a thousand: the largest early medieval burial ground ever found in Wales. For at least two weeks of the dig, the Home Office licence to remove the dead has run out. The work goes on.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/

### VII.15 (81). 28 July 1994 — Who owns the dead

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19940728-1 · Date: 1994-07-28 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Museum record

In July 1994 Ideal Homes, as owner of the land, gives the human remains and finds to the National Museum of Wales. Finds belong to whoever owns the land. So the merged title decides, once more, who owns what came out of Parcel A. The dead of St Dochdwy's pass from a developer to the state.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.16 (82). 1994 – 96 — Church View Close

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19941110-1 · Date: 1994-11-10 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

In November 1994 the Forest of Cardiff's title to the woodland, the half of Parcel A the family say was taken in 1955, is registered. The power lines go in. The houses go up. Church View Close is built over the farm, and new titles are carved out of the merged one, house by house.

> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Mary's heirs · never adjudicated, never extinguished · woodland now registered to the Forest of Cardiff (WA735527) · land to the south a village green
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": WA231076 and the house titles carved from it (Church View Close)

- Wiki page: Woodland — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings
- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/

### VII.17 (83). 2005 — The cemetery in print

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-20050101-1 · Date: 2005-01-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

In 2005 the cemetery is published in a learned journal: 1,026 burials. It tells the story of the dead. It does not tell the story of the family whose home stood over them, or of how that home came down.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Publication: Holbrook and Thomas, Medieval Archaeology 49 (2005) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Wiki page: Woodland — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/

### VII.18 (84). 20 March 2019 — Nearly thirty years late
