Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-20190320-1 · Date: 2019-03-20 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Heritage record

In 2019 GGAT's 1990 report on Great House Farm is finally added to the national record, nearly thirty years after it was written, and thirty years after the house was gone.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### VIII.1 (85). November 2025 – January 2026 — The grandchildren

Act VIII: The Buried Title · Scene id: ghf-20251117-1 · Date: 2025-11-17 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Official correspondence

In November 2025 Mary's grandchildren start digging for the buried title. The community council says it cannot help. Cadw's email addresses bounce, the first of many. In January 2026 they ask the Land Registry to put back on the register the claim that was left off it in 1983.

> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Mary's grandchildren · application to the Land Registry, January 2026

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.2 (86). February – March 2026 — "No evidence of a mistake"

Act VIII: The Buried Title · Scene id: ghf-20260323-1 · Date: 2026-03-23 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

The Land Registry retrieves its old paper files. In March it replies: there is 'no evidence of a mistake in the register'. It treats the farm as one holding, exactly as the 1916 tenancy did. It does not say how the house got into BP's title.

> The words: "no evidence of a mistake in the register" — The register treats the farm as one holding, exactly as the 1916 wording did.
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — 2026 complaint — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026
- Official correspondence: HMLR holding letter, 13 February 2026 (PDF) — https://github.com/unclehowell/datro/blob/wayback/wayback/pdf/foi/2026-02-13_hmlr_wa231076_holding-letter.pdf

### VIII.3 (87). 19 April – 25 May 2026 — "Registered correctly"

Act VIII: The Buried Title · Scene id: ghf-20260419-1 · Date: 2026-04-19 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

The family complain. The Registry will not look behind the 1987 judgment. In May it rules that the title is 'registered correctly'. It is relying on a judgment about possession to answer a question about ownership: the same substitution the whole scheme was built on.

> The words: "registered correctly" — Correct only if a judgment about possession can answer a question about ownership.
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": Land Registry, May 2026: 'registered correctly'

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — 2026 complaint — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026

### VIII.4 (88). 21 May 2026 — Cadw's two photographs

Act VIII: The Buried Title · Scene id: ghf-20260521-1 · Date: 2026-05-21 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

Cadw releases its two photographs from July 1988, marked 'YYY': 'marginally below the bar', it says. Everything else is gone. The file is 'quite likely' destroyed, it says; by July, 'most likely'. There is no record of anyone destroying it.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/
- Analysis: Cadw — Forensic Critique — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/cadw-forensic-critique-v8-0-0/
- Photograph: Cadw survey photograph of the farmhouse, 29 July 1988 (released 2026, ATISN 27021) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/foi-reply-register/#R37

### VIII.5 (89). June – July 2026 — The missing root

Act VIII: The Buried Title · Scene id: ghf-20260730-1 · Date: 2026-07-30 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

In June the family ask to see the Registry's original files, and ask that nothing be destroyed. Six months after their first request, the Registry lists the forty-three documents behind BP's first registration. The 1969 conveyance, the root BP's title recites, is not among them. Neither is any deed that carries the house from Bute, or from the Thomases, or from the Williamses, to anyone.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — 2026 complaint — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026

### VIII.6 (90). 25 August 2026 — "Not held"

Act VIII: The Buried Title · Scene id: ghf-20260825-1 · Date: 2026-08-25 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Official correspondence

Museum Wales refuses the family's request: the information is 'not held'. In the same letter it says it has found records of other discoveries at Great House Farm, and withholds them as 'not in scope'.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.7 (91). 8 September 2026 — A lead to 1877

Act VIII: The Buried Title · Scene id: ghf-20260908-1 · Date: 2026-09-08 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

Glamorgan Archives hold no deed for the 1877 sale. But they point to the Bute trustees' book of payments for that year, now in Cardiff. If Daniel Thomas paid Bute for the house, it will be written there: the first link of the true chain, in Bute's own hand.

- Official correspondence: The 1877 Agreement — Glamorgan Archives reply — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#glamorgan-2026-4097b

### VIII.8 (92). 17 – 21 September 2026 — Complaints

Act VIII: The Buried Title · Scene id: ghf-20260917-1 · Date: 2026-09-17 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

In September the family lodge a formal complaint against Cadw, whose own address blocks it. They write to their MP, Stephen Doughty, asking for the Parliamentary Ombudsman. They ask Heneb, the successor to GGAT, for its files. A Land Registry agent tells them the title was 'closed in 2005', which the Registry's own history contradicts.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/
- Wiki page: The Restoration Campaign — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/restoration-campaign/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — 2026 complaint — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026

### VIII.9 (93). 23 September 2026 — The Lords papers

Act VIII: The Buried Title · Scene id: ghf-20260923-1 · Date: 2026-09-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

The National Archives finds the House of Lords papers in BP Properties v Buckler, added to its catalogue only in May 2026. For thirty-eight years, searches had found nothing.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.10 (94). 25 – 27 September 2026 — An offer on the woodland

Act VIII: The Buried Title · Scene id: ghf-20260925-1 · Date: 2026-09-25 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

The Forest of Cardiff, which holds the woodland cut from Parcel A, offers the family a route to owning it, on its own terms. They turn it down. You do not buy back what was never yours to sell.

- Wiki page: Woodland — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/
- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.11 (95). 27 – 29 September 2026 — Keep everything

Act VIII: The Buried Title · Scene id: ghf-20260927-1 · Date: 2026-09-27 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

The family take the Land Registry to its Independent Complaints Reviewer, and complain to Heneb about GGAT's part from 1982 to 1995. A preservation notice goes to eleven public bodies: keep everything.

- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/
- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.12 (96). 29 September – 5 October 2026 — On record all along

Act VIII: The Buried Title · Scene id: ghf-20260929-1 · Date: 2026-09-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

The Royal Commission opens its archive: the 1974 newspaper report, and an old note of the soldier in armour under the dining-room floor. Museum Wales, after two refusals, releases its file on the bones found by the church in 1858. The story was on record all along.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### VIII.13 (97). September – October 2026 — The question

Act VIII: The Buried Title · Scene id: ghf-20261006-1 · Date: 2026-10-06 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Analysis

The family put everything they have found in public: every document and every cutting, from the geese of 1891 to the bus of 1989. And they ask the one question that no court, no registry and no minister has ever answered: by what deed did the house pass from the Williamses, or from anyone, to BP? No such deed has ever been produced.

- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/
- Wiki page: Great House Farm Wiki — Main Page — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/
- Wiki page: Evidence Library — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/
- Wiki page: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/
- Wiki page: Press Articles Index — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### E.1 (98). Today — How it was done

Epilogue: Today · Scene id: ghf-99990101-1 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Analysis

So here is how it was done. Not with one forged deed, but with a sequence. First, two words in 1916 made two parcels one farm, in a landlord's document, never the family's. Then six attempts to make Mary's occupation of her own house look permissive: her house spoken of as part of her husband's fields tenancy; an order against the fields tenant worded for the whole farm; a tenancy offered, and refused; a possession order made and left in a drawer; another tenancy offered, and refused; and a licence she never asked for and never accepted. Alongside them, the woodland and the land to the south were taken from around her. Then the paper: BP took the fields by deed and the case against the house with them; one BP company conveyed the house to another; the state registered it, then folded it into the fields. The family, for their part, were led into claiming adverse possession of the mythical farm, counted from an order about the fields, when Parcel A had been theirs since 1928 and by possession since 1940. And the courts, asked only who had the right to possession, never had to ask who owned the house. In English law, possession can be awarded without ownership ever being tried, and a title can be registered without any court deciding a rival claim to the same land. Neither step, on its own, decides the older title. Every move went through one of those two doors.

- Wiki page: The Two Parcels — the title test — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/the-two-parcels/
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### E.2 (99). Today — Who knew

Epilogue: Today · Scene id: ghf-99990101-4 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Analysis

So who knew the farm was two? Mary did, in her way. Her 1974 statement tells of the house and ten acres sold to Daniel Thomas, and the nine acres Bute kept. But her deeds were gone, and no lawyer of hers ever turned that history into a case about two parcels. If the family had grasped what it meant, they would have shouted it from the rooftops; it was their whole case. The other side never needed it explained. Western Ground Rents offered tenancies of "the farmhouse and garden" alone, and sued for it alone. BP conveyed it alone, between its own companies, registered it alone, and then merged it. The Land Registry issued two titles and joined them into one. The Court of Appeal read a conveyance of "the farmhouse and garden". Everyone made a mess of this case: the drafting, the lawyers, the courts, the Registry. A haze over the two parcels might be forgiven once. But the people who knew best treated the two parcels as one whenever that helped, and as two whenever that helped more. The family call it what it looks like: a conspiracy against them.

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The Two Parcels — the title test — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/the-two-parcels/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — two titles, then one — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

### E.3 (100). Today — Who holds it now

Epilogue: Today · Scene id: ghf-99990101-2 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Analysis

Today twenty houses stand on Great House Farm, on titles carved from the merged one. BP has sold up and gone. The Land Registry says the title is 'registered correctly'. A thousand of Llandough's dead lie in the stores of the National Museum. The woodland belongs to a charity. The house is gone, and so is the heritage file that might have saved it. And underneath all of it lies the true Parcel A: Vaughan, Bute, Daniel Thomas, Williams. Buried. Never decided. Never extinguished.

- Wiki page: Where Things Stand — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/
- Wiki page: Missing Records Register — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/missing-records-register/

### E.4 (101). Today — Not in the history

Epilogue: Today · Scene id: ghf-99990101-3 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Public record

The village's own history page tells of the Roman villa, the lost monastery, and the hundreds of burials dug up in 1994. It does not mention the Great House, the family who lived in it for three hundred years, or the morning it was bulldozed. There has been no public inquiry. No apology. No reparation.

- Public record: Llandough Community Council — About Llandough — https://www.llandough-cc.co.uk/About_Us_20117.aspx
- Wiki page: Where Things Stand — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/

### E.5 (102). Today — What the family ask for

Epilogue: Today · Scene id: ghf-99990102-1 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family case

The family ask for what was taken. A ruling, at last, on who owns Parcel A. The woodland and the green back, or reparation where that cannot be done. Reparation for the houses built on their land. The estate's artefacts returned. A true record of the Great House in the nation's heritage. And a public inquiry into how all of it was allowed to happen. Every body involved is being given the chance to put it right, before the family go back to court.

- Wiki page: Family Reparations & Remedy Roadmap — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/family-reparations-remedy-roadmap/
- Wiki page: Where Things Stand — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/
